candidates.title: Live tuning: in-headset tuning of design tokens and skin values with export back to the assets that own them
candidates.objective: Define an engine-light tuning model (a closed tunable kind set of float, int, bool, enum, colour, vector2, and vector3; an immutable registry populated by explicit registration; set, reset, reset-all, snapshot, apply, and export intents on an immutable state with deterministic replay; and a bridge to and from the design-language token JSON) and a Unity adapter (explicit binding records to skin assets, live apply through the existing skin seams with diagnostics, an injectable export sink whose device JSON and Editor asset writers let a Play-mode or on-device change survive, and a tuning panel that is one client of the XR UI shell with a UGUI fallback), so a developer wearing the headset changes a colour, size, corner radius, or spacing and sees the effect immediately, and the change lands in the asset that owns it instead of in a rebuild loop; the family proves the plumbing, and whether a value looks right on a device stays a Device Lab receipt.
source_requirements: Official engine documentation for runtime-editable serialized values, ScriptableObject assets, Play-mode change loss, and the Editor asset-writing APIs at the version pinned by the compatibility profiles

Maintained public runtime tuning implementations (an immediate-mode tweak panel and a runtime inspector with one typed drawer per kind) with license, maintenance state, and an immutable review ref confirmed by a person

The repository's own design-language token standard, skin seams, Settings contract, and XR UI shell contract as the seams the family composes on, with the rule that it introduces no second token vocabulary
Evidence boundaries that route every legibility, colour, size, and comfort judgement to a Device Lab receipt, so no package claim says a tuned value is correct on a headset
candidates.exact_next_action: A person confirms the URLs, page paths, and version pins in docs/standards/live-tuning/source-manifest.json and admission.draft.json; then run the cross-project admission gate on the draft and decide whether the tuning model, the binding and export seams, and the panel-as-shell-client rule are stable enough to admit a Core blueprint and one Unity adapter blueprint.
